target.title: fix(whatsapp): use canonical media primitives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp maintained local copies of outbound media loading, audio transcoding, MIME classification, and base64 validation even though canonical media owners already existed. The copies had drifted: injected media readers could silently widen local-file access, image optimization was not forwarded through the shared loader, and malformed base64 uploads could reach permissive decoding.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves WhatsApp onto the existing canonical media paths and deletes its local outbound-media loader.

- Outbound loading now uses `plugin-sdk/outbound-media`; the shared facade only gains forwarding for its already-supported `optimizeImages` option.
- Voice transcoding now uses the existing `transcodeAudioBufferToOpus`; the helper only gains typed output-container and maximum-duration options so WhatsApp can preserve Ogg/Opus output and its duration cap.
- MIME normalization and classification now use the existing `plugin-sdk/media-mime` helpers.
- Upload buffers now use the existing SDK base64 estimator and strict canonicalizer before decoding.

WhatsApp-specific behavior stays local: MP3, M4A, and WebM inputs still transcode; only Ogg/Opus is accepted directly as a voice note; document naming remains transport-specific; and the legacy retry helper is intentionally untouched.

The final diff is deliberately narrow: 12 files, 184 additions, and 185 deletions. It touches only WhatsApp and the two existing shared owners that needed small typed/forwarding additions.

## User Impact

Supported WhatsApp media sending and voice-note behavior remain unchanged. Injected media readers must provide an explicit local-root boundary. Malformed WhatsApp upload buffers are rejected by strict base64 canonicalization, and configured size limits are enforced from the encoded-size estimate before allocating the decoded buffer.

## Evidence

- 113 focused tests passed across WhatsApp, audio transcoding, and the outbound-media SDK facade.
- Core and extension TypeScript checks passed.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` passed without adding an SDK entry point.
- The full build passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29662927176
- Fresh autoreview against the actual PR base reported no accepted or actionable findings.

## Live WhatsApp QA (2026-07-19 UTC)

- Local isolated execution with the linked `default` driver and `work` SUT accounts using `mock-openai`.
- Tested head: `4e875a0cf177f2d4764309464246cf8e16664238`; exact comparison base: `649e94dd21705d8996468026e5e037d4c18f4942`.
- Complete 52-scenario first pass: 51 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped.
- The single focused rerun reproduced `whatsapp-reply-to-mode-batched` at the missing batched-reply quote assertion.
- Exact-base comparison with retries disabled reached the same assertion and failed, so this is not branch-specific regression evidence.
- Production state database guard remained unchanged; the installed Gateway was already failed before QA and was left in that pre-existing state. Its service definition was preserved.
- Redacted artifacts: `.artifacts/qa-e2e/whatsapp-full-pr-refactor-whatsapp-canonical-media-4e875a0cf177-20260719T050148Z/`; exact-base artifacts: `.artifacts/qa-e2e/whatsapp-full-sha-commit-649e94dd2170-649e94dd2170-20260719T063447Z/`.
